name: A Third Companion Blocks a Pair in VC Dimension Three
statement: Let $G$ be a nonempty cornerless ample family of VC dimension at most three. Suppose three distinct missing tips $c,u,v$ give ample individual extensions with the same three-coordinate acquired support $I$, and $u=c^{\{i\}}$, $v=c^{\{j\}}$. Then neither $G\cup\{c,u\}$ nor $G\cup\{c,v\}$ is dismantlable ample.
proof: The punctured cubes at $c,u$ complete the four-cube on $P=I\cup\{i\}$ when both tips are added. The third punctured cube supplies an outside neighbor to every non-corner vertex on the $c$ side. Any old corner of the pair extension must lie in this completed four-cube and have no outside neighbor; the only possible first deletions therefore lie among its upper antipode and the three adjacent upper vertices. Deleting either new tip first leaves a one-corner extension and then the cornerless family, so it cannot start a full peeling. Once an old vertex is deleted, the support $P$ leaves the shadow, and every subsequent ample subfamily has VC dimension at most three. Degree and missing-square arguments protect all twelve vertices on the lower side, the two tips, and their three upper neighbors; only the four candidate upper vertices can ever be deleted. They cannot exhaust the family, so no peeling exists. Interchanging $u$ and $v$ gives the second conclusion.
comments: The fixed VC-three control has 1,761 concepts and a complete 15-state negative certificate. A VC-four control isolates the step where the dimension bound is used but remains nonpeelable for an independent proper-minor reason.
